basis: Price return unless labelled total return (dividends excluded). Baseline Nov 4, 2024 close (session before the election). Nov 2024 is the post-election partial period Nov 5–29 only; Nov 2026 is month-to-date through Nov 18.

meta.event: Donald Trump elected for second presidential term
meta.inauguration: Jan 20, 2025 (market closed, MLK Day; split uses Jan 17, 2025 close)
meta.vol_definition: Annualised realised volatility = std dev of daily returns within the month x sqrt(252) x 100
meta.nov2024_note: Nov 2024 is the post-election partial period Nov 5-29 only, not a full calendar month
meta.dow_tr_note: Dow Jones total-return index (^DJITR) has only 1 day of history on Yahoo Finance; Dow total return is NOT available - price return only, dividends excluded and disclosed.
meta.ndx_tr_note: Nasdaq-100 total return NOT shown: Yahoo ^NDXT is unreliable. Its ratio to the price index whipsaws (0.514 Nov 2024, 0.489 Dec 2024, 0.498 Dec 2025, 0.605 Jun 2026, 0.540 Nov 2026) instead of rising smoothly with dividends, and implies impossible monthly dividend gaps (Apr 2026 +7.8pp, May 2026 +9.2pp, Jun 2026 +5.1pp). A true TR/price ratio rises monotonically by the dividend yield (~0.7%/yr for NDX). NDX is shown price-only.
meta.spx_tr_note: S&P 500 total return from ^SP500TR is valid: TR/price ratio rises smoothly and monotonically (2.190 Nov 2024, 2.195 Dec 2024, 2.223 Dec 2025, 2.246 Nov 2026), implying ~1.3%/yr dividends.

lag1.note: No lag effect in either direction.

correlations.yoy_note: YoY windows overlap (12-month rolling), so read the YoY correlation as a description of the trend divergence, not a clean statistical estimate; the MoM correlation is the cleaner read.
